{{eastern name order|Cser Krisztián}}
'''Krisztián Cser''' (pronounced [kristiaːn t͡ʃɛr]) (born 9 December 1977) is a Hungarian operatic and concert singer ([[Bass (voice type)|bass]]) and [[physicist]], the soloist of the [[Hungarian State Opera]].

== Biography ==
Krisztián Cser was born in 1977, in [[Szeged]], [[Hungary]]. He grew up in a family of musicians. His grandmother Tímea Cser was a soprano, grandfather Gusztáv Cser was a composer-conductor, father [[:hu:Cser Miklós|Miklós Cser]] was a conductor. His mother [https://balloandrea.jimdofree.com/ Andrea Balló] is a painter. He has 5 siblings. One of his brothers, [[:hu:Cser Ádám|Ádám Cser]] is a musician too, he is a composer-conductor. He grew up in [[Szeged]], [[Hungary]], where he began his musical studies by playing the [[piano]] in his early childhood. After leaving high school, he graduated in physics at the [[University of Szeged]] in 2002 ([[Hungary]]) and began to work as a PhD student at the [[Biological Research Centre (Hungarian Academy of Sciences)|Institute of Biophysics of the Szeged Biological Research Centre]]. But his artistic roots proved strong, science was replaced by music in his life. He studied classical singing at the [[University of Szeged]], where his vocal trainer was István Andrejcsik, then he attended the Department of Vocal and Opera Studies at the [[Franz Liszt Academy of Music|Liszt Academy]], where the famous operatic singer [[Éva Marton]] was his professor and studied stage movement and acting with Balázs Kovalik.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.proscenium.at/|title=PROSCENIUM International Artists Management|first=Proscenium Artist's Management|last=GmbH|website=PROSCENIUM}}</ref>
[[File:Krisztian Cser opera singer 2020 photo Zsofi Raffay 02.jpg|left|thumb|302x302px|Cser in February of 2020]]
Krisztián Cser succeeded in several Hungarian and international singing competitions, either he got into the finals, got a special prize, or even won.

He came out as an oratorio soloist in [[Johann Sebastian Bach|J. S. Bach]]'s [[St John Passion|Saint John Passion]] in 1998. His repertoire includes a wide range of musical styles from early [[baroque music|baroque]] to [[contemporary music]]. In opera roles he appeared first in 2008, since when he has been a member of the [[Hungarian State Opera]]. His first lead role at the [[Hungarian State Opera]] was Pomádé in [[György Ránki|Ránki]]'s King Pomádé's New Clothes. He has sung under the baton of renowned Hungarian and foreign conductors such as [[Pierre Cao]], [[Péter Eötvös]], [[Helmuth Rilling]], [[Peter Schreier]], [[Muhai Tang]], [[:hu:Hollerung Gábor|Gábor Hollerung]], [[Kirill Karabits]], [[Zoltán Kocsis]], [[Ádám Fischer]], [[Iván Fischer]], [[Zoltán Peskó]], [[György Vashegyi]], [[Ken'ichiro Kobayashi]], [[Zsolt Hamar]] and [[Tamás Vásáry]]. During the years, his title-role singing in [[Béla Bartók]]'s [[Bluebeard's Castle]] became emblematic, he sings it in many Hungarian and international performances successfully with the contribution of renowned conductors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://operavilag.net/interjuk/kulcskeresesben-cser-krisztiannal-het-ajton-at/|title=Kulcskeresésben Cser Krisztiánnal – hét ajtón át|date=February 6, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bfz.hu/en/media/bfo-magazine/cser-i-dont-usually-decide-ahead-of-time-what-kind-of-prince-i-will-be/|title=Cser: "I don't usually decide ahead of time what kind of prince I will be"|website=Budapest Festival Orchestra}}</ref><ref>[https://bachtrack.com/review-senza-sangue-bluebeard-eotvos-mupa-budapest-february-2018 Bachtrack, 11 Febr 2018]</ref> In some of the countries during his tour around the world, the audience could listen to and watch this opera for the first time in his performance. Above all, on the CD published in 2018 for the centenary of the [[Bluebeard's Castle]] premiere, Krisztián Cser sings [[Bluebeard]].

Besides [[Bartók]]'s opera, he has played other remarkable roles on opera stages. He frequently sings the bass roles of [[Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart|Mozart]]'s operas as Figaro, Leporello and Sarastro, and authentically plays the protagonists in [[Giuseppe Verdi|Verdi]] and [[Richard Wagner|Wagner]]'s operas, such as The Grand Inquisitor and Philip II in [[Don Carlos]] or Wotan in [[Das Rheingold|The Rhinegold]]. His other leading roles have included Colline in [[Giacomo Puccini|Puccini]]'s [[La bohème]] and Don Basilio in [[Gioachino Rossini|Rossini]]'s [[The Barber of Seville]]. His ever-expanding repertoire includes more than 60 operas and nearly 80 roles.

He regularly performs on Hungarian opera and concert stages. He gave recitals also at the [[Royal Festival Hall]] in [[London]], at the [[Elbphilharmonie]] in [[Hamburg]] and many more famous concert hall. He has debut as Wotan in [[Richard Wagner|Wagner]]'s [[Das Rheingold|The Rhinegold]] in 2018, and as Don Pizarro in [[Ludwig van Beethoven|Beethoven]]'s Fidelio at the [[Theater Chemnitz|Opernhaus Chemnitz]]. In 2019 he sang the role of Bluebeard with the [[Budapest Festival Orchestra]] conducted by Iván Fischer, at [[Carnegie Hall]] in [[New York City]]. He also sang the role of Wotan in the fall of 2019 in [[Mexico City]], where the 150th anniversary of the staging of [[Richard Wagner|Wagner]]'s [[Das Rheingold|The Rhinegold]] was celebrated.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://papageno.hu/featured/2019/10/cser-krisztian-wagnernek-mexikoban-is-van-letjogosultsaga/|title=Cser Krisztián: "Wagnernek Mexikóban is van létjogosultsága"|date=October 31, 2019|website=Papageno}}</ref>
